subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should the remaining fix path require an out-of-process or restart-aware cron failure signal, or is in-Gateway restart accounting plus diagnostics sufficient once memory growth is proven fixed?
rationale: The code already has partial in-process recovery, but the issue specifically reports failureAlert being silent when the same Gateway process is starved; deciding whether to add a separate watchdog/reporting surface is a product and operations boundary choice.

options.title: Require soak plus restart-aware alert design
options.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer-led macOS launchd soak proof and a design that surfaces started-without-success cron failures even when the Gateway process is unhealthy.

options.title: Split the remaining work
options.body: Track memory/RSS growth and cron failure reporting as separate canonical items if maintainers want narrower ownership and validation lanes.

options.title: Accept current recovery only
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept that v2026.6.11 diagnostics and restart accounting are the intended behavior and provide macOS soak proof showing memory no longer grows.

recommendation.title: Require soak plus restart-aware alert design
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer-led macOS launchd soak proof and a design that surfaces started-without-success cron failures even when the Gateway process is unhealthy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available owner for the cross-cutting runtime/product decision because the remaining question spans cron, Gateway availability, and maintainer validation policy.
